name: Valle de Uco

climate: A dry climate, though much of its little rain falls while the vines grow. Water is scarce.

keyfacts: The Uco Valley is a notable sub-region of Mendoza, which produces more than 60% of Argentine wine.
Argentina's most highly rated Malbec comes from the high-altitude districts of Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley, in Andes foothills between 2,800 and 5,000 feet.
In the high-altitude vineyards of Tupungato, in the Uco Valley, Chardonnay is increasing in popularity.
High altitude and low humidity mean Argentine vineyards rarely face insects, fungi or mold, so growers can use little or no pesticide.

blurb.text: A wine area in Mendoza, Argentina's leading wine province, with San Carlos, Tupungato and Tunuyán inside. Malbec dominates plantings at 55%, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon (10%) and Chardonnay (7%).
